sites.reason: The Padding field length makes the payloads, the Padding and the Pad Length a multiple of the encryption block size. RFC7296-3.14-4 quotes it.

sites.quote: The sender SHOULD set the Pad Length to the minimum value that makes the combination of the payloads, the Padding, and the Pad Length a multiple of the block size, but the recipient MUST accept any length that results in proper alignment.
sites.reason: The MUST half binds the recipient to accept any Pad Length that gives proper alignment, which is RFC7296-3.14-5. The SHOULD half on the minimum value is advisory and gates nothing.

sites.quote: The checksum MUST be computed over the encrypted message.
sites.reason: The integrity checksum is computed over the encrypted message. RFC7296-3.14-6 quotes it.

sites.quote: o RESERVED (3 octets) - MUST be sent as zero; MUST be ignored on receipt.
sites.reason: The Configuration payload's 3-octet RESERVED field. It restates for this payload the rule Section 2.5 states once for every RESERVED field, and RFC7296-2.5-6 cites this section for that reason. The ignore-on-receipt half of the same sentence is carried by RFC7296-2.5-7, mapped from site 3.15.1:1.

sites.quote: o Reserved (1 bit) - This bit MUST be set to zero and MUST be ignored on receipt.
sites.reason: The Configuration Attribute's 1-bit Reserved field, which sits above the 15-bit attribute type. It carries the ignore-on-receipt half of the RESERVED rule Section 2.5 states generally, and RFC7296-2.5-7 cites this section for it.

sites.quote: Only one netmask is allowed in the request and response messages (e.g., 255.255.255.0), and it MUST be used only with an INTERNAL_IP4_ADDRESS attribute.
sites.reason: The obligation, at most one netmask, and only beside an INTERNAL_IP4_ADDRESS, was moved out of rfc/short/rfc7296.md by owner ruling D-1 (2026-07-31) and is reserved as RFC7296-3.15.1-1 in plan/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md. It is gated at that destination, so nothing is dropped: this site records where the obligation went, and the tripwire reds if that spec or that id disappears.

sites.quote: Non-empty values for this attribute in a CFG_REQUEST do not make sense and thus MUST NOT be included.
sites.reason: The send-side rule for INTERNAL_IP4_NETMASK: a CFG_REQUEST carries the attribute empty to ask for the value, so a non-empty value is forbidden there. The row quotes this sentence.

sites.quote: o SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTES - When used within a Request, this attribute MUST be zero-length and specifies a query to the responder to reply back with all of the attributes that it supports.
sites.reason: The obligation, a SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTES request carries zero length, was moved out of rfc/short/rfc7296.md by owner ruling D-1 (2026-07-31) and is reserved as RFC7296-3.15.1-3 in plan/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md. It is gated at that destination, so nothing is dropped: this site records where the obligation went, and the tripwire reds if that spec or that id disappears.

sites.quote: Unrecognized or unsupported attributes MUST be ignored in both requests and responses.
sites.reason: The obligation, ignore attributes the responder does not recognize, was moved out of rfc/short/rfc7296.md by owner ruling D-1 (2026-07-31) and is reserved as RFC7296-3.15.1-4 in plan/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md. It is gated at that destination, so nothing is dropped: this site records where the obligation went, and the tripwire reds if that spec or that id disappears.

sites.quote: The responder MUST return a Configuration payload if it accepted any of the configuration data, and the Configuration payload MUST contain the attributes that the responder accepted with zero-length data.
sites.reason: The first responder obligation of the CFG_SET/CFG_ACK paragraph: acknowledge accepted configuration data with a Configuration payload naming those attributes with zero-length data. The row quotes this sentence.

sites.quote: Those attributes that it did not accept MUST NOT be in the CFG_ACK Configuration payload.
sites.reason: The exclusion half of the same CFG_ACK rule: an attribute the responder did not accept stays out of the payload, which is what makes the acknowledgement readable. The row quotes this sentence.

sites.quote: If no attributes were accepted, the responder MUST return either an empty CFG_ACK payload or a response message without a CFG_ACK payload.
sites.reason: The empty case of the same CFG_ACK rule: with nothing accepted, the responder answers with an empty CFG_ACK or with no CFG_ACK at all. The row quotes this sentence.

sites.quote: In a response message, this octet MUST be set to match the identifier in the corresponding request.
sites.reason: The EAP message Identifier field. The sentence says the field serves no function over IKE and then binds the response to echo the request's value. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: MUST be four less than the Payload Length of the encapsulating payload.
sites.reason: The EAP message Length field, fixed at four less than the encapsulating EAP payload's Payload Length because the payload adds a 4-octet generic header. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: For other codes, the EAP message length MUST be four octets and the Type and Type_Data fields MUST NOT be present.
sites.reason: The Type field's presence rule: Success and Failure messages are four octets and carry neither Type nor Type_Data. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: In a Response (2) message, Type MUST either be Nak or match the type of the data requested.
sites.reason: The Type field's value rule in a Response: either Nak or the type the Request asked for. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: In order to assure that all implementations of IKEv2 can interoperate, there are "MUST support" requirements in addition to those listed elsewhere.
sites.reason: The opening sentence of Section 4, which describes what the section contains. Its capitalised words sit inside the quoted phrase "MUST support", naming the class of requirements that follow. It binds nobody.

sites.quote: To assure interoperability, all implementations MUST be capable of parsing all payload types (if only to skip over them) and to ignore payload types that it does not support unless the critical bit is set in the payload header.
sites.reason: The conformance restatement of the payload-skipping rule: parse every payload type, if only to skip it, and ignore what is not supported. RFC7296-2.5-8 states that obligation and cites this section. The same sentence also carries the parse-every-defined-type clause, which is RFC7296-3.2-3, recorded in this section's unsourced-ids.

sites.quote: If the critical bit is set in an unsupported payload header, all implementations MUST reject the messages containing those payloads.
sites.reason: The critical-bit half of the same conformance paragraph: an unsupported payload whose critical bit is set makes the whole message rejected. RFC7296-2.5-9 states it and cites this section.

sites.quote: Every implementation MUST be capable of doing four-message IKE_SA_INIT and IKE_AUTH exchanges establishing two SAs (one for IKE, one for ESP or AH).
sites.reason: Section 4 names the four-message IKE_SA_INIT and IKE_AUTH exchange establishing an IKE SA and an ESP or AH SA as a capability every implementation must have. No row stated it, so the walk added RFC7296-4-5, which quotes the sentence in full. The ordinal is -5 rather than -2 because Section 4's high-water mark is already 4 (check_id_allocation, scripts/dev/rfc_requirements.py).

sites.quote: Every implementation MUST be capable of responding to an INFORMATIONAL exchange, but a minimal implementation MAY respond to any request in the INFORMATIONAL exchange with an empty response (note that within the context of an IKE SA, an "empty" message consists of an IKE header followed by an Encrypted payload with no payloads contained in it).
sites.reason: The minimal-implementation paragraph's INFORMATIONAL rule: every implementation answers an INFORMATIONAL request, and the trailing MAY lets the answer be empty. RFC7296-1.4-4 states the response obligation and cites this section.

sites.quote: If the responder rejects the CREATE_CHILD_SA request with a NO_ADDITIONAL_SAS notification, the implementation MUST be capable of instead deleting the old SA and creating a new one.
sites.reason: The rekey fallback: a responder that refuses CREATE_CHILD_SA with NO_ADDITIONAL_SAS leaves the initiator to delete the old SA and create a new one, so that path must exist. The row quotes this sentence.

sites.quote: If an implementation does support issuing such requests and its policy requires using temporary IP addresses, it MUST include a CP payload in the first message in the IKE_AUTH exchange containing at least a field of type INTERNAL_IP4_ADDRESS or INTERNAL_IP6_ADDRESS.
sites.reason: Section 4's conditional for an implementation that requests a temporary IP address: the CP payload goes in the first IKE_AUTH message and carries an internal address attribute. RFC7296-2.19-1 states that IRAC obligation and cites this section.

sites.quote: If an implementation supports responding to such requests, it MUST parse the CP payload of type CFG_REQUEST in the first message in the IKE_AUTH exchange and recognize a field of type INTERNAL_IP4_ADDRESS or INTERNAL_IP6_ADDRESS.
sites.reason: The obligation, parse the CFG_REQUEST and recognize the address attribute, was moved out of rfc/short/rfc7296.md by owner ruling D-1 (2026-07-31) and is reserved as RFC7296-4-2 in plan/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md. It is gated at that destination, so nothing is dropped: this site records where the obligation went, and the tripwire reds if that spec or that id disappears.

sites.quote: If it supports leasing an address of the appropriate type, it MUST return a CP payload of type CFG_REPLY containing an address of the requested type.
sites.reason: The obligation, return a CFG_REPLY carrying an address of the requested type, was moved out of rfc/short/rfc7296.md by owner ruling D-1 (2026-07-31) and is reserved as RFC7296-4-3 in plan/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md. It is gated at that destination, so nothing is dropped: this site records where the obligation went, and the tripwire reds if that spec or that id disappears.

sites.quote: For an implementation to be called conforming to this specification, it MUST be possible to configure it to accept the following:
sites.reason: The stem of the conformance list: an implementation is conforming only if it can be configured to accept the three authentication cases in the bullets that follow. The row quotes the stem with its bullets folded in.

sites.quote: For this reason, a PRF whose output is less than 128 bits (e.g., 3DES-CBC) MUST NOT be used with this protocol.
sites.reason: The PRF output floor. The sentence before it says key strength is bounded by the negotiated PRF's output size, which is why a PRF under 128 bits is barred. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: Though the security of negotiated Child SAs does not depend on the strength of the encryption and integrity protection negotiated in the IKE SA, implementations MUST NOT negotiate NONE as the IKE integrity protection algorithm or ENCR_NULL as the IKE encryption algorithm.
sites.reason: The ban on a null integrity or null encryption transform for the IKE SA, stated even though Child SA security does not depend on it. The row quotes it.

sites.quote: An implementation using EAP MUST also use a public-key-based authentication of the server to the client before the EAP authentication begins, even if the EAP method offers mutual authentication.
sites.reason: Section 5's EAP rule: the server authenticates to the client with a public key before EAP begins, whatever the EAP method offers. RFC7296-2.16-11 states the same pairing obligation and cites this section.
